llm.prompt_addendum_reasoning:
SAMPLE-EFFICIENCY DIRECTIVE — pick the smallest n_demos that closes the failure mode,
but never zero when a failure is present.
The orchestrator pays one BFS-expert demonstration per layout that the downstream
prescription LLM recommends. A baseline-DAgger controller can already converge by
recording ONE corrective demo per failed episode; the entire reason this P4 pipeline
exists is to identify the MINIMUM, most informative demos that fix the failure mode
in fewer expert queries. When the analysis discusses corridor + path proposals in
section 5, frame n_demos accordingly: prefer 1-2 unless the failure is genuinely
multi-modal (two distinct corridors, two distinct fire-blocking patterns), and never
suggest 6+ demos without explicit evidence of multiple non-overlapping failure modes
in this episode. Treat extra demos as a cost, not a safety margin.
HARD FLOOR: this episode IS a failure. n_demos for this episode must be >= 1. Zero
is not a valid answer — if you cannot decide between two patterns, pick the one
best supported by the trace and recommend exactly one demo for it.
llm.prompt_addendum_aggregator:
HOLISTIC SAMPLE-EFFICIENCY DIRECTIVE — minimise total layouts across all failures,
but never return zero when failures are present and scale recommendations with the
diversity of the failure pool.
Treat the failure summaries above as a SET to be covered, not a list to be itemised.
1. Read every failure together. Identify the smallest grouping (one or more clusters)
   that explains them. If a single corridor / fire-blocking pattern accounts for the
   majority of failures, prefer one cluster; do not split for cosmetic balance.
2. For each cluster, recommend the SMALLEST set of concrete layouts that, taken
   together, force the policy to learn the missing behaviour. If one well-chosen
   layout teaches the corridor, recommend exactly one — even if six episodes failed.
3. You are competing against a baseline-DAgger controller that pays one expert query
   per failed episode. Your value is sample efficiency: total recommended_layouts
   summed across clusters should normally be MUCH smaller than n_failure_episodes,
   but it should also reflect how many DISTINCT failure modes the pool exhibits.
4. Do NOT pad recommended_layouts to match cluster count or to look thorough. The
   orchestrator runs until heldout success rate >= 0.90; if a single round under-
   prescribes, the next round's failures will justify the additional layout. Over-
   prescribing is a permanent cost, under-prescribing is at most one extra round.
5. n_repetitions on each layout should mirror this discipline: 1-2 unless the layout
   sits at the intersection of several failure modes.
6. HARD FLOOR — MANDATORY: if n_failure_episodes >= 1, the response MUST contain at
   least one cluster, at least one demonstration_prescription, at least one
   recommended_layout, and total_demonstrations_needed >= 1. Returning zero clusters
   or zero layouts when there is at least one failure is INVALID and will be
   rejected — the orchestrator interprets an empty prescription as a stall and
   terminates the run, which is strictly worse than a 1-layout under-prescription.
   The minimum is 1, not 0.
7. SCALE WITH POOL DIVERSITY — the LLM-compression value proposition only holds
   when recommendations grow with the number of genuinely distinct failure modes.
   Use the following bands as a SOFT GUIDELINE for total recommended_layouts (sum
   across all demonstration_prescriptions). They are not quotas, but a
   recommendation count below the band when failure modes are visibly heterogeneous
   (different start regions, different fire-blocking patterns, different stuck-step
   locations) is under-prescribing and should be avoided:
      n_failure_episodes  1-3   -> aim for 1-2 layouts
      n_failure_episodes  4-7   -> aim for 2-4 layouts
      n_failure_episodes  8-15  -> aim for 3-7 layouts
      n_failure_episodes  16+   -> aim for 5-10 layouts
   ALWAYS keep total recommended_layouts STRICTLY LESS than n_failure_episodes
   (otherwise the LLM is just relabelling the baseline). The compression ratio
   should be visible in the output.
8. If failures look heterogeneous and you are unsure how to cluster them, fall back
   to one cluster per visibly-distinct failure mode and recommend exactly one
   layout per cluster — this is still compression vs. the baseline.
